Barrett Welcomes Secretary Burgum and Speaker Johnson to Mid-Michigan | Representative Tom Barrett Skip to main content Phone:  (202) 225-4872 Email Me Address:  1232 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC 20515   Barrett Welcomes Secretary Burgum and Speaker Johnson to Mid-Michigan August 19, 2026 Press Release Image Lansing, Mich. — Yesterday, Congressman Tom Barrett welcomed U.S. Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum and Speaker of the House Mike Johnson to mid-Michigan to highlight the hard work of local residents in research, manufacturing, and construction. Barrett and Burgum toured Michigan State University’s Facility for Rare Isotope Beams (FRIB), which is receiving $125 million in federal investments Congressman Barrett  secured earlier this year. They also both participated in the grand opening at LG Energy Solution in Lansing. Barrett and Johnson then toured the ongoing Tower on Grand construction, which will be a mixed-use skyscraper with housing and commercial units. “Exciting things are happening every day across mid-Michigan that will continue to support new opportunities and growth in our communities — from cutting-edge rare isotope research to historic development that will make housing more affordable and revitalize our downtown,”  said Barrett. “In Congress, I've taken action to lower costs for Michigan workers, create opportunities for manufacturing and engineering, and make it easier to build affordable homes for Michigan families. It was great to have Secretary Burgum and Speaker Johnson here to see the progress happening in my district thanks to the innovation and work ethic of the people I have the honor to represent.” “Great to be hosted by Congressman Barrett in the Great Lake State to see firsthand the Facility for Rare Isotope Beams (FRIB), which demonstrates the importance of investing in cutting-edge research, advanced technologies and preparing the next generation to strengthen America's energy future - innovation made possible with the help of the Working Families Tax Cuts Act,”  said Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum. “The U.S. needs more highly trained American workers capable of develop

Barrett Hosts Fifth Interactive Town Hall With 14,700 Participants Across Mid-Michigan | Representative Tom Barrett Skip to main content Phone:  (202) 225-4872 Email Me Address:  1232 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC 20515   Barrett Hosts Fifth Interactive Town Hall With 14,700 Participants Across Mid-Michigan August 18, 2026 Press Release Washington, D.C. —  Tonight, Congressman Tom Barrett (MI-07) hosted a successful interactive town hall with more than 14,700 constituents from across Michigan’s 7th Congressional District. This is Barrett’s fifth interactive town hall since taking office, which has allowed him to connect with more than 34,000 constituents no matter where they are. “My job is to be mid-Michigan’s representative in Washington — not Washington’s representative in mid-Michigan,”  said Barrett.  “The best way I can do that is by hearing directly from the people I serve, and I’ve spent the summer on the road meeting with thousands of hardworking people to talk about real issues and hear their stories to help me do the real work back in Washington to improve their lives. I will keep fighting on behalf of every mid-Michigander to make our community safer, more prosperous, and a better place to raise a family.” During tonight’s hour-long event, Barrett provided an update on his recent work in the House of Representatives, including his  votes and legislation to limit the military conflict in Iran . He also spoke about his recent travels throughout the district to hear directly from families, business owners, farmers, workers, and more about the issues that matter to them. The congressman also took questions on a wide range of issues, including his stance on the USS Abraham Lincoln, data centers, North Korea, Medicaid, and more. BACKGROUND: In the last 4 weeks, Barrett has traveled throughout Michigan’s 7th District to meet with constituents from all walks of life. He has visited dozens of locations across mid-Michigan, including local businesses, hospitals, colleges, factories, farms, and more. Barrett Introduces Bills to Protect Local Communities from Data Center Overreach | Representative Tom Barrett Skip to main content Phone:  (202) 225-4872 Email Me Address:  1232 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC 20515   Barrett Introduces Bills to Protect Local Communities from Data Center Overreach August 20, 2026 Press Release Image Washington, D.C. —  Congressman Tom Barrett (MI-07) today introduced legislation to ensure every community in Michigan and across the United States maintains their autonomy over the decision-making process related to building a data center. Specifically, the two bills would protect local control by prohibiting the federal government from overriding local zoning decisions and banning members of Congress from signing non-disclosure agreements related to data center projects. The introduction of the legislation was first reported in  The Detroit News . “People in mid-Michigan are tired of big corporations and politicians negotiating backroom deals, especially when it comes to data center projects that impact every community differently,”  said Barrett.  “Families in my district are rightly concerned about the effect data centers could have on their utility bills, as well as the land and water in their neighborhood. They deserve to know all the facts and have the final say over any proposed project. That starts with stopping federal overreach and preventing the secrecy pledges that have plagued Michigan and undermined the power of local residents.” Barrett has long opposed the government putting a thumb on the scale in favor of data centers. When he served in the Michigan House of Representatives, he  voted   against legislation his own party passed to give corporate welfare for data center construction and equipment purchases. Below is additional information on the two bills Congressman Barrett introduced: The  Protecting Local Control of Data Centers Act ( H.R. 10119 ) would prohibit federal agencies from overriding local land-use, zoning, siting, or permitting authority related to data centers. Barrett Hears About Agriculture, Education, and Transportation During Week of Meetings Across Mid-Michigan | Representative Tom Barrett Skip to main content Phone:  (202) 225-4872 Email Me Address:  1232 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC 20515   Barrett Hears About Agriculture, Education, and Transportation During Week of Meetings Across Mid-Michigan Image August 14, 2026 Press Release Lansing, Mich. — Congressman Tom Barrett (MI-07) this week met with hardworking mid-Michiganders in agriculture, education, and transportation to hear from them about the issues that matter to their families and local businesses. Throughout the week, Barrett toured local farms, held a roundtable discussion on free and fair agricultural trade, learned about research on crops and mobility technology at Michigan State University, visited a tutoring center, and hosted U.S. Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy for conversations about infrastructure and transportation. “Meeting directly with mid-Michiganders, seeing their work firsthand, and hearing about their needs is the most important part of my job,”  said Barrett. “This week, I appreciated listening to farmers, educators, scientists studying crop diseases and developing vehicles, local transportation leaders, and other hardworking residents. These helpful and informative discussions enable me to better represent the people of our communities and make sure their voices are heard in Washington.” Image On Monday, Barrett visited Certain League Farms in Williamston and met with Mike and Roseann Bills, who raise asparagus, sunflowers, corn, horses, and puppies. The Billses have a daughter with special needs, and they founded the farm with a vision to offer adults with special needs the opportunity to reach their full potential and work a job that gives them dignity and purpose. Image Barrett then visited the Plant Pathology Field Laboratory at Michigan State University and met with scientists who are conducting critical research to help farmers across mid-Michigan and the United States manage and mitigate crop diseases. The officials held a roundtable with local leaders, toured the Capital Region International Airport, and visited Dean Transportation in Lansing. Transportation issues have been a top priority for Barrett, who successfully  secured $15.3 million for mid-Michigan infrastructure projects,  supported the BUILD America 250 Act to maintain and strengthen federal infrastructure and transit funding programs, and  led efforts to  make air travel safer after the tragic January 2025 collision over Reagan National Airport in Washington, D.C. “Whether flying across the country or driving to work across town, mid-Michiganders deserve safe, reliable transportation,”  said Barrett. “That’s why I’ve been working in Congress and with the Trump administration to invest the people’s tax dollars in local infrastructure that makes a difference. I’m proud to have Secretary Duffy in Lansing to hear about the work our communities are putting in to fix our roads and bridges to continue making transportation safer and smoother.” “Michiganders are fortunate to have Representative Barrett advocating on their behalf in Congress. The bill would require a qualified, licensed health care professional, exercising independent clinical judgment, to make any decision that a particular procedure, treatment, or prescription is not medically necessary. “Artificial intelligence should never replace the judgment of a doctor,” said Barrett. “When it comes to someone’s health and well-being, the outcome is too important to leave it up to an algorithm. This bill makes sure doctors — not AI — remain responsible for determining what care patients need while bringing greater transparency to the use of these technologies in health insurance.” “When a computer system is making decisions about health care, people will get hurt,” said Landsman. “We have to make sure health care professionals remain the decision makers.
